### Scope

A key is bound to one MCPJam organization at creation and acts
**as you,\ninside that organization**. Per-request authorization still applies: a call\nonly succeeds if the key's owner can acces

s that project and server. A key
can never reach projects outside its organization.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two deliberate restriction

s while in preview:
>
> * **API keys cannot manage API keys.** Requests to the key-management surface
> with an `sk_…` bearer
fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revoke keys in\n> the UI.\n> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API.** Sign in to create k

eys.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an API key like a password:

* Load it from an environment variable or secret manager — ne
ver commit it to\n source control or ship it in client-side code.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integration, named so you c
an tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating a replacement key, switching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n* If a key leaks, revo

ke it immediately in
 [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

If you see `401 UNAUTHORIZED` with
`details.reason: \"ORPHANED_KEY\"`, the key\nis no longer bound to an organization and cannot be used — create a new key\nfrom [S

ettings](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

## Conventions

**Requests.** Operations on servers are `POST` with a JSO
N body (most accept\nan empty `{}`). **Reads** — the catalog listings and eval-run polling — are\n`GET` and take their options (`c

ursor`, `limit`, filters) as query
parameters.

**Responses.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind | Shape |
|
- | - |\n| Single resource | The resource object directly |\n| Collection | `{ \"items\": [...], \"nextCursor\": \"...\" }` — `ne
xtCursor` omitted on the last page |\n| Error | `{ \"code\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\", \"details\": {...} }` with a matching

HTTP status |

**Pagination.** Collections are cursor-based. Pass the previous response's
`nextCursor` as `cursor` in the next

request (body field on `POST` lists,
query parameter on `GET` lists). Cursors are opaque — don't parse them.

**Authoring vs ru
nning suites.** `POST /eval-suites` creates a runnable suite\n(the suite plus its test cases) **synchronously** and responds `201`
with the\n`suiteId`, WITHOUT running anything — author once, run later. `POST /eval-runs`\nis the async counterpart: it validates
and creates a run synchronously, then\ndetaches execution and responds `202` with a `runId`. Poll\n`GET /eval-runs/{runId}` until

`status` is `completed`, `failed`,
`cancelled`, or `timed_out`.

**IDs.** Every identifier the API takes is discoverable throu
gh the API\nitself: `GET /projects` lists your projects, `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers`\nlists each project's servers, and `G

ET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites`
lists its eval suites. Start from `GET /me` to confirm which account a key
acts as.

##

Errors

Errors always use the canonical body `{ code, message, details? }`. The `code`
is stable and machine-readable; `message

` is human-readable and may change;
`details` is an optional, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `U
NAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Missing, invalid, revoked, or orphaned key |\n| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP server** needs an O
Auth grant — distinct from a bad key |\n| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | 403 | The **target MCP server** allowed the connection and asked for s
ign-in on this call. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge. Your key is fine — see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-ch
allenges) |\n| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Key is valid but not allowed to do this — or the **target MCP server** rejected the credentials
MCPJam presented (retrying with a different MCPJam key will not help; reconnect or re-authorize the server) |\n| `VALIDATION_ERRO
R` | 400 | Malformed body or parameters |\n| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown project, server, or resource |\n| `CONFLICT` | 409 | The
resource isn't in a state that accepts this write — a stale `expectedRevision`, a duplicate name, or an environment that can't cur
rently be launched. Re-read and retry |\n| `FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` | 422 | The target server doesn't support this MCP capability |
\n| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests — see [Rate limits](#rate-limits) |\n| `SERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502 | Could not connect
to the target MCP server |\n| `TIMEOUT` | 504 | The target MCP server connected but didn't respond in time |\n| `INTERNAL_ERROR`

| 500 | Something failed on our side |

New error codes may be **added** over time; treat unknown codes as
non-retryable failur

es unless the HTTP status says otherwise.

### Sign-in challenges

Some MCP servers allow the connection and ask for sign-in o

nly on a protected
call. The API never starts a sign-in. It reports the challenge instead:

* **HTTP 401 from the MCP server**
on `tools/call`: the API answers\n `403 AUTH_REQUIRED`. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge:\n its `source` (`h
ttp_401`), and the `error`, `requiredScope`, and\n `resourceMetadataUrl` the server sent, when present.\n* **An `isError` result
carrying `_meta[\"mcp/www_authenticate\"]`** (the\n ChatGPT convention): the call succeeds, and the `CallToolResult` is returned\
n unchanged with an additive `authChallenge` field (`source:\n \"tool_result_meta\"`). A field the server already set under that

name is never
 overwritten.

`AUTH_REQUIRED` is not `UNAUTHORIZED`: your MCPJam key is fine, so a different
key will not hel
p. Complete the OAuth flow for that server yourself, upload the\ntoken to one of its [accounts](#server-accounts), and call again.

See
[Mid-session sign-in](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/lazy-authentication.md).

## Rate limits

Each key gets **60 req
uests per minute** sustained, with bursts up to **10**.\nExceeding it returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (in\n

seconds):

```http theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 7

{ "code": "RATE_LIM

backoff, and expect these limits
to be tuned during the preview.

Other `429`s — the per-minute brakes and daily budgets descr
ibed with the\nendpoints below — carry `Retry-After` whenever the refusal knows when it\nlifts, which is the ordinary case. Treat
it as a hint that is usually there\nrather than a guarantee: a refusal that reaches you without one still needs\nyour backoff, so

**never** block waiting for a header that may not come.

## Endpoints

Each endpoint is fully documented — request and respons

e schemas, examples,
and an interactive playground — under **Endpoints** in the sidebar.

**Catalog** — discover the IDs everyt

hing else takes:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET /me` | The account behind the key |
| `GET /organizations` | T
he organizations the caller belongs to — where `organizationId` comes from. A key is bound to one organization and only ever sees
that one |\n| `GET /projects` | Projects the key can access (optionally `?organizationId=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/server
s` | The project's saved MCP servers |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions` | A server's stored revisions,
newest first: captures of its tools and server info, recorded whenever they change (`?limit=&cursor=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projec
tId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}` | One revision: every tool's definition and the server info it reported. Field
s listed in `droppedFields` were too large to store, so they are unknown, not absent |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serv
erId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}/diff` | What changed since the revision before, or since `?from=`: tools added, removed and chang
ed, and server info changes with both values. A field listed in `droppedFields.from` or `droppedFields.to` was not stored on that
side, so a change to it is unknown |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites` | The project's eval suites, with latest-run summa
ries |\n| `GET`, `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients` | List clients, or create one from a template or full config |\n| `GET`, `PA
